The basic problem for these robots is separation, requiring all the robots with the same color to separate from the other robots, each group forming a recognizable geometric shape (e.g., circle, point, line); this task must be performed in finite time, in spite of the robots being unconscious of their own color, unable to communicate, and oblivious. This problem has been studied and solved in the synchronous setting (SSS 2023). In this paper we show that the problem is solvable also under the more difficult asynchronous adversary, provided the robots agree on the orientation of one axis, and no robot is uniquely colored. The proof is constructive: we present a distributed algorithm that allows unconscious colored robots with one-axis agreement to separate into parallel lines under the asynchronous scheduler.

articleTitle: A QA-Assisted Job Scheduler for Minimizing the Impact of Urgent Computing on HPC System Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: In recent years, there has been an increase in large-scale natural disasters such as earthquakes, tsunamis, and storms, raising the importance of disaster prevention and mitigation. Thus, extensive studies on urgent computing use High Performance Computing (HPC) systems for rapid simulations and prompt countermeasures. To meet the deadlines of urgent jobs, job schedulers may have some features so that urgent jobs could have a higher priority of execution than other jobs. As a result, urgent job execution could have negative impacts on the execution of other jobs with lower priorities and, hence, on overall HPC system operation. The goal of this paper is to efficiently execute urgent jobs to meet their deadlines while minimizing the negative impacts on HPC system operation. This paper assumes that some of the running jobs can be suspended (and resumed later) to immediately execute an urgent job. Another important assumption is that there is a possibility that the suspended job could be terminated if necessary to meet the deadline, and thus its intermediate computation results are lost if the total memory usage of urgent and suspended jobs exceeds the memory capacity. The proposed method employs quantum annealing or quantum-inspired annealing (QA) techniques to find an appropriate combination of jobs to be suspended so as to minimize the loss of computational results while meeting the deadlines of urgent jobs. The evaluation results show that the proposed method can properly select an appropriate combination of jobs to be suspended so that it can minimize the computational losses. The results also demonstrate that the superiority of the proposed method becomes more remarkable in practical situations where the power-saving feature of HPC systems is enabled.

articleTitle: NUSS:Non-Interactive Updatable of Secret Sharing Schemes Using Homomorphic Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: Secret sharing schemes (SSS) are essential for distributed cryptography due to their role in safeguarding sensitive data. They face significant challenges in maintaining longterm security, especially in dynamic environments that require frequent updates to shares, such as in cloud storage systems where data is continually modified and accessed by multiple parties. While proactive secret sharing (PSS) addresses this issue through periodic share renewal, current methods necessitate extensive inter-party communication, resulting in high bandwidth usage and increased vulnerability to synchronization attacks. Moreover, these interactive update processes risk leaking sensitive information, including threshold structures. Motivated by these challenges, we propose NUSS (Non-Interactive Updatable Secret Sharing), a novel approach leveraging homomorphic encryption for non-interactive updates of secret shares. Our method encrypts shared arrays homomorphically, enabling share updates within the encrypted domain without requiring share regeneration and redistribution. Specifically, the update process is conducted via homomorphic computation, which works directly on the ciphertext. This approach ensures data security and minimizes communication complexity, allowing each party to complete the update process independently using encrypted share arrays. Experimental evaluation confirms that NUSS effectively mitigates the risk of information leakage compared to traditional proactive secret sharing. Additionally, our proposal requires only n secure channels, significantly reducing communication costs by lowering the number of secure channels required from O(n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) in traditional PSS to O(n).

articleTitle: A Learning-based Control Scheme for Prioritized SMT Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: In Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) processors, multiple threads share hardware resources, which improves the overall utilization of the pipeline, but reduces the throughput due to stalls caused by hardware resource shortage and instruction retention of low-priority threads. In real-time processing, where tasks are processed based on priority, high-priority threads occupy much of the processor pipeline, resulting in lower total throughput compared to SMT which does not use priority.In this paper, we propose a novel learning-based SMT processor for real-time processing. This processor dynamically changes its priority according to the utilization of hardware resources. The proposed processor has a mechanism for autonomous learning and inference, which enables dynamic control in response to resource demand bottlenecks and their changes. There are two inference methods suitable for hard and soft real-time systems. It also learns autonomously to make more optimal predictions. Each functional unit of the proposed processor has a counter that indicates the amount occupied at a particular time, the rate, and the total value. The counter allows learning and inference based on resource utilization, throughput, and instruction loss rate. This allows the overall throughput to be increased without compromising the real-time performance of high-priority threads and allows resources to be allocated to other threads. In addition, simulation results show that the IPC (instructions per clock) rate is higher in soft real-time systems, where high throughput is required in multiple applications.

articleTitle: Matthiola incana classification using CNN and class activation maps for model understanding
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: In the production of seedlings for flowers and vegetables, selective differentiation is widely performed for only seedlings with high market-value prospects; however, many tasks require specialized knowledge. Mistakenly discarding seedlings with high market value leads to economic losses for farmers, making it crucial to provide a reliable system that also explains the basis for differentiation. This study proposes a method for the reliable classification of Matthiola incana (M. incana) by utilizing neural network-based image classification, supported by visualizing class activation maps to provide evidence for differentiation. Additionally, the study introduces the MiLIC (Matthiola incana Leaf Image Classification) dataset, developed for use in training the classification model. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Kentaro-Machida/Matthiola-incana-Leaf-Image-Classification.

articleTitle: Isogeny-based Proxy Signature
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: Proxy signatures are protocols used when a signer wishes to delegate their ability to sign. The original signer will delegate its signing right to a proxy signer, who will then be able to output a proxy signature on the original signer’s behalf. In this paper, we propose an isogeny-based proxy signature by using the Commutative Supersingular Isogeny-based Fiat-Shamir signature (CSI-FiSh) as a basis. We prove the resulting proxy signature scheme is EUF-CMA-CWA in the Quantum random oracle model. We then compare our scheme to the base signature.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Recognition System Using DNN Accelerator with Multi-threading on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: In this paper, we implement a stand-alone facial expression recognition system on an SoC FPGA with multi-threading using a Deep learning Processor Unit (DPU). The system consists of two steps: one for face detection step and one for facial expression recognition. In the previous work, the Haar Cascade detector was run on a CPU in the face detection step due to FPGA resource limitations, but this detector is less accurate for profile and variable illumination condition images. Moreover, the previous work used a dedicated circuit accelerator, so running a second DNN inference for face detection on the FPGA would require the addition of a new accelerator. As an alternative to this approach, we run the two inferences by DNN on a DPU, which is a general-purpose CNN accelerator of the systolic array type. Our method for face detection using DenseBox and facial expression recognition using CNN on the same DPU enables the efficient use of FPGA resources while maintaining a small circuit size. We also developed a multi-threading technique that improves the overall throughput while increasing the DPU utilization efficiency. With this approach, we achieved an overall system throughput of 25 FPS and a throughput per power consumption of 2.4 times.

articleTitle: LoS Trick: Countermeasure against CPA for DNN Models Using Loss of Significance in Multiply-Accumulate Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: The recent advancements in deep neural network (DNN) models have revolutionized image recognition, natural language processing, and healthcare. However, deploying DNN models in IoT devices introduces significant security risks, particularly side-channel attacks such as correlation power analysis (CPA). In this paper, we introduce a novel countermeasure named loss of significance (LoS) trick LoS trick is designed to protect DNN models from CPA attacks by reducing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) during the multiply-accumulate operations. We reduce information leakage in power consumption traces by adding large absolute values in the initial stages of multiply-accumulate operations. LoS trick increases the difficulty of obtaining accurate weight parameters. This paper details the theoretical foundation of LoS trick and its implementation methodology and validates its effectiveness through simulations. The results demonstrate that LoS trick outperforms conventional countermeasures, providing a scalable solution to enhance the security of DNN models in IoT environments.

articleTitle: AGV-Assisted Construction of Dynamic Wi-Fi Fingerprint Databases for Indoor Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: Wi-Fi fingerprinting has become a dominant technology for indoor localization because it does not require additional hardware or new infrastructure. However, the construction of fingerprint databases remains one of its major challenges because collecting a large number of fingerprints over service areas is not only labor-intensive but also time-consuming. The high labor and time cost becomes even more challenging for the construction of dynamic fingerprint databases to deal with the time-varying nature of wireless channels indoors, where Wi-Fi Received Signal Strength Indicators (RSSIs) are to be measured at the same Reference Points (RPs) repeatedly. To address these issues, Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV)-assisted construction of dynamic fingerprint databases is proposed in this paper. As it is assumed that users use their smartphones for indoor localization service, a smartphone is mounted on an AGV and used to collect Wi-Fi RSSIs every 10s as the AGV moves along a pre-arranged path with reference points marked with tag36h tag family for AprilTag 3. Then, the locations of the collected RSSIs are aligned to those of the tags based on the time information of both AGV and smartphone. The analyses based on the AGV-collected data on the three floors of the XJTLU IR building and the corresponding data from the XJTLU dynamic database, the latter of which are jointly collected by human participants and wallmounted Raspberry Pi Pico Ws, demonstrate that the proposed AGV-assisted construction of dynamic fingerprint databases can be used in complex indoor environments and reduce the high labor and time cost of the manual data collection without impairing the indoor localization performance.

articleTitle: Alter Ego: Identifying Web Server Certificates Containing IP Addresses As Subjects
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: This study is concerned with the security implications of Web IP certificates, a particular category of web server certificates in which the subject is represented by an IP address in place of a fully qualified domain name (FQDN). Web IP certificates permit clients to verify the server in question by means of its IP address; however, they also present a number of significant risks. In particular, if a Certificate Authority (CA) issues a Web IP certificate without adequately verifying the server’s ownership or usage rights of the IP address, it could permit unauthorized third parties to obtain certificates for IP addresses they do not control. To date, no comprehensive survey has been conducted to examine the prevalence and characteristics of such certificates. To address this gap in the paper, we conducted a large-scale survey, establishing TLS connections to all IPv4 addresses, with the objective of collecting certificates and analyzing the presence and features of Web IP certificates.

articleTitle: Bounded unpopularity matching in a (3, 3)-hypergraph with one-sided preferences
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: We solve the following problem: given two sets of different items and a set of people with combined preferences over pairs of items, one from each set, what is the best way to match the pair of items to the people? To solve this problem, we consider the popular matching problem in a 3-uniform 3-partite hypergraph, where the first set comprises agents, while the second and third sets contain distinct items respectively. Agents have preferences over the hyperedges, whereas the members of the other sets lack such preferences. An agent votes for a matching in which he/she obtains a better assignment. A matching M is called popular if there is no matching M' such that the number of agents that prefer M' is more than the number of agents that prefer M. Finding a popular matching, if it exists, is a hard problem. Therefore, one approach is to find a matching that is approximately popular. The usual metric in this case is called the unpopularity factor of a matching M, denoted by u(M). In this paper, we provide an approximation algorithm that produces a matching M in a 3-uniform 3-partite hypergraph such that $u(M) \leq 1.5 \times {3^{\frac{k}{2}}}$ where k is the maximum degree of an agent. The approximation algorithm takes O(k(n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.5</sup> + m)) time to produce the matching M where n is the total number of agents and m is the total number of hyperedges. In a 3-uniform 3-partite hypergraph where k is a constant, our algorithm performs well and produces a matching M with u(M) = O(1). Importantly, our approach stands as the inaugural algorithm to achieve a bounded unpopularity matching in a hypergraph.

articleTitle: Parallel GPU Computation of Nuclear Attraction Integrals in Quantum Chemistry
publicationTitle: 2024 Twelfth International Symposium on Computing and Networking Workshops (CANDARW)
abstract: In quantum chemical calculations, methods such as Hartree-Fock and density functional theory are used to numerically solve the Schrödinger equation. These methods require the pre-computation of nuclear attraction integrals, which represent the integrals over the attraction of an electron from all nuclei. This study presents a novel approach to accelerate the calculation of nuclear attraction integrals using Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). To optimize GPU performance, we employ three main strategies. First, we enhance the recursive relations of the Obara-Saika and McMurchie-Davidson methods, which are commonly used algorithms for these calculations, to leverage GPU acceleration. Second, we implement a hybrid approach, selecting either the Obara-Saika or McMurchie-Davidson method based on the specific types of computed integrals. Finally, we utilize the CUDA stream to parallelize the execution of GPU kernels, efficiently utilizing the available multicore processors on the GPU. Experimental results on various molecules demonstrate that our proposed method achieves up to 1635 times faster computation than a CPU implementation.
